name: The corpus at risk
note: CATASTROPHE events. The mechanic the whole game is built around rested on fourteen events and one fire. Loss needs its counterweight or the ledger only ever goes one way, so recovery events are here too — Aluvihare, Xuanzang, Atisha, the Tibetan and Chinese canons, the bhandaras, and the nineteenth-century recoveries. NOT specialist-reviewed.

events.title: Taxila's schools do not recover
events.evidence: Destruction levels at Sirsukh and the disappearance of the site from later Chinese pilgrim accounts that had described it as a centre.
events.note: The northwest's scholarly centre ends and the corpus loses a whole transmission route.

events.title: Valabhi sacked; the university ends
events.evidence: The abrupt end of the Maitraka grant series, and the silence of later sources about a place Xuanzang had described as holding six thousand monks.

events.title: Nalanda sacked; Vikramashila and Odantapuri follow
events.evidence: Persian chronicles written for the victors; a destruction layer at the site; and the negative evidence of texts surviving only in Tibetan and Chinese.

events.title: Vikramashila is destroyed
events.evidence: Tibetan accounts of the flight of scholars, and the site's abrupt archaeological end.

events.title: Odantapuri is destroyed
events.evidence: Persian and Tibetan accounts; the site is poorly excavated and the date is inferred from the campaign sequence.

events.title: Somapura is abandoned
events.evidence: Burn layers and the end of occupation at Paharpur; the cause is not established.

events.title: Jagaddala ends and its scholars go to Tibet
events.evidence: Tibetan colophons naming Jagaddala scholars arriving; the monastery itself was only located in the twentieth century.

events.title: The Odishan diamond triangle monasteries wind down
events.evidence: Declining construction and endowment at Ratnagiri, Lalitagiri and Udayagiri; a slow ending rather than a fire.

events.title: Kashmiri Sanskrit libraries are dispersed
events.evidence: Later Kashmiri accounts of manuscript loss; how much is contemporary record and how much later lament is hard to separate.
events.dispute_text: The scale of loss under the Sultanate is described very differently by different later sources, some of which have a position to defend. The event is real; its magnitude is argued.

events.title: Vijayanagara is sacked after Talikota
events.evidence: The ruins themselves, which show systematic destruction, and contemporary Persian and Portuguese accounts.

events.title: Nagarjunakonda's monasteries are abandoned
events.evidence: End of occupation and endowment in the excavated sequence.

events.title: Amaravati's stupa is quarried for building stone
events.evidence: Company records of the removal, and the sculptures now distributed between Chennai, London and elsewhere.
events.note: Not destruction by an invader. A local zamindar wanted lime and an antiquarian wanted marbles.

events.title: Sarnath is quarried for a canal
events.evidence: Jagat Singh's removal of the stupa's brick, recorded by contemporaries who arrived too late to stop it.

events.title: A generation of palm leaf reaches the end of its life
events.evidence: The material itself: palm leaf survives roughly three centuries in Indian humidity, so every surviving text is a copy of a copy.
events.note: Not an event anyone recorded. It is the standing condition the whole corpus economy exists to answer.

events.title: Most Vedic shakhas cease to be recited
events.evidence: The schools are named in the ritual literature and almost none survive; the loss is visible only as a list of names with nothing attached.

events.title: Further recitation schools fall silent
events.evidence: Comparison of the shakha lists in successive ritual manuals, which shorten.

events.title: The Brihatkatha survives only through its retellings
events.evidence: The original Paishachi text is lost; three later Sanskrit versions describe what they are adapting.

events.title: Most of the Sangam corpus is lost before it is collected
events.evidence: The anthologies themselves reference poets and works that do not survive; what exists was recovered in the nineteenth century.

events.title: The Ajivika canon disappears entirely
events.evidence: The school is described in detail by Buddhist and Jain opponents and not one of its own texts survives.
events.note: A whole philosophical tradition known only through the people who disagreed with it.

events.title: The materialist texts are lost
events.evidence: Quoted only to be refuted. The Tattvopaplavasimha is the sole substantial survival and it is late.

events.title: Aryabhata's other work does not survive
events.evidence: Later commentators cite an Aryabhatasiddhanta that no longer exists.

events.title: The Bakhshali manuscript survives incomplete
events.evidence: The birch-bark leaves themselves, found in fragments in a field in 1881 and radiocarbon-dated across several centuries.

events.title: Bengal's climate destroys manuscripts faster than they are copied
events.evidence: Survival rates: almost nothing on palm leaf survives from eastern India before the eleventh century, and a great deal survives from drier Rajasthan.

events.title: Insects and rodents take what damp does not
events.evidence: The precautions themselves: manuscript chests, neem leaves, turmeric and the recopying schedules that assume loss.

events.title: Kerala's manuscript tradition keeps recopying and most of it still goes
events.evidence: Surviving palm-leaf collections against the works their own colophons reference.

events.title: Kalibangan shows what is read as earthquake damage
events.evidence: Displaced walls and a fault trace beneath the site.
events.dispute_text: The seismic interpretation is one reading of the structural damage; subsidence and abandonment have both been proposed instead.

events.title: Kot Diji burns
events.evidence: A burnt layer between the Early and Mature Harappan levels.
events.dispute_text: Whether the fire marks conflict, an accident, or a deliberate ritual closing of a settlement phase is argued, and the same layer appears at other sites.

events.title: Coastal Gujarat sites are lost to the sea
events.evidence: Submerged structures off the Saurashtra coast.
events.dispute_text: Both the dating and the identification of the submerged remains are contested, and the subject attracts claims well beyond the evidence.

events.title: Pataliputra's timber walls burn
events.evidence: Excavated timber palisade with burning; Megasthenes had described the walls as wooden.

events.title: An earthquake destroys towns across the Himalayan front
events.evidence: Persian chronicle accounts and later palaeoseismic trenching along the Himalayan frontal thrust.

events.title: A great storm and shock strike Bengal
events.evidence: European trading records; the casualty figures that circulated were later shown to be inflated by an order of magnitude.
events.dispute_text: Contemporary reports conflate a cyclone with an earthquake said to have struck the same night. Modern seismology finds no evidence of a large earthquake, and the event as usually described probably did not happen.

events.title: The Allah Bund earthquake reshapes Kutch
events.evidence: Company survey records and the fault scarp itself, which dammed a river and created a lake.

events.title: The Assam earthquake
events.evidence: Geological Survey of India investigation, one of the earliest scientific earthquake studies anywhere.

events.title: The Bihar-Nepal earthquake
events.evidence: Instrumental records and the government relief reports.

events.title: Fire destroys much of Surat
events.evidence: Company records of the fire and of the merchant records lost with the warehouses.

events.title: Manuscript collecting begins under the Company
events.evidence: The founding of the Asiatic Society and the collection registers that follow.
events.note: Displacement is not destruction, and the distinction matters mechanically: a work that leaves survives.

events.title: The Mackenzie collection removes thousands of manuscripts
events.evidence: The collection catalogue, which lists what was gathered and from where.

events.title: The Thanjavur palace library passes into state hands
events.evidence: The transfer records; the collection survived where many private ones did not.

events.title: The Bower manuscript is bought from a treasure-seeker
events.evidence: Hoernle's edition and the account of its purchase in Kucha.

events.title: Indian texts surface at Dunhuang, having survived outside India
events.evidence: The Dunhuang cave library and its dispersal to London, Paris, Beijing and St Petersburg.
events.note: The clearest proof the game's central mechanic is right: what left survived.

events.title: The Gilgit manuscripts are found in a stupa
events.evidence: The find itself, among the oldest surviving Buddhist manuscripts anywhere, preserved by being sealed and forgotten.

events.title: Partition divides libraries and archives
events.evidence: Records of the division of the imperial collections, and the losses in transit and in the violence.

events.title: Last use of the Indus script
events.evidence: The seals and inscribed objects themselves, absent from all later levels. It remains undeciphered.
events.replaces: Last use of the Indus script

events.title: Prakrit literature is eclipsed and mostly lost
events.evidence: Prakrit works survive largely in Jain collections; the secular corpus is known from references.

events.title: Paishachi ceases to be written at all
events.evidence: No text in the language survives; it is known only from grammarians' descriptions and the Brihatkatha tradition.

events.title: The Digambara-Svetambara split leaves each without the other's canon
events.evidence: Each tradition's account of what the other lost; the Digambaras hold the original canon to be gone entirely.

events.title: Buddhist institutions in the south lose patronage and their libraries with them
events.evidence: The Manimekalai and later Tamil Buddhist works survive; the institutions that held them do not.

events.title: Jain institutions lose royal favour in the Tamil country
events.evidence: Shaiva hagiography celebrates it, which is evidence of the tradition and not of the events it describes.
events.dispute_text: The impalement of eight thousand Jains at Madurai appears first in hagiography centuries later and is not corroborated. That Jain institutions lost patronage is well supported; the massacre is not.

events.title: Sectarian disputes destroy rival institutions' records
events.evidence: Inscriptional erasures and re-dedications, which are physical and visible on temple walls.

events.title: Inscriptions are chiselled out by successors
events.evidence: The erasures themselves, which usually leave enough to read what was removed.
events.note: The record's own record of being edited.

events.title: The Pali canon is committed to writing at Aluvihare
events.evidence: The Sri Lankan chronicles, and the fact that the canon exists.
events.note: A deliberate redundancy decision taken against a foreseen risk. It worked.
events.replaces: Pali canon written down at Aluvihare

events.title: Xuanzang leaves with six hundred and fifty-seven texts
events.evidence: His own travel account, his translation corpus, and the Chinese canon.

events.title: Atisha leaves Vikramashila for Tibet
events.evidence: Tibetan and Bengali records of his journey and teaching.
events.note: Fifty years before Vikramashila was ash, and what he carried was not.

events.title: The Tibetan translation project preserves what India loses
events.evidence: The Kangyur and Tengyur, which contain hundreds of works whose Sanskrit originals are gone.

events.title: The Chinese Buddhist canon preserves lost Sanskrit works
events.evidence: The translations themselves, dated and attributed, many of originals that no longer exist.

events.title: Nambi Andar Nambi recovers the Tevaram hymns
events.evidence: The Chola-period tradition of the recovery and the arrangement that followed it.

events.title: The Alvar hymns are collected and arranged
events.evidence: Srivaishnava tradition credits Nathamuni; the traditional dates are impossible as stated.

events.title: Jain merchant capital funds the bhandara libraries
events.evidence: The bhandaras at Jaisalmer, Patan and Cambay, and their catalogues.
events.note: Much of what survives from western India survives because merchants paid to keep it dry.

events.title: The Jain canon is fixed in writing at Valabhi
events.evidence: The Svetambara tradition's account of the council and the recension that follows it.

events.title: Mahinda carries the canon to Sri Lanka
events.evidence: The Sri Lankan chronicles and the Mahavihara tradition.

events.title: The Thanjavur collection is catalogued and kept
events.evidence: The Maratha rulers' cataloguing of the palace library, which is why it survived.

events.title: Printing begins to make loss reversible
events.evidence: Serampore and Fort William press output; a printed text can be lost from every library and still exist.
events.note: The first technology in seven thousand years that breaks the link between a work and its carriers.

events.title: U. V. Swaminatha Iyer recovers the Sangam corpus from palm leaf
events.evidence: His own account of the search, and the editions that followed.
events.note: Most of classical Tamil literature was three decades from being unreadable.

events.title: A national manuscript survey begins to count what is left
events.evidence: The government manuscript search reports, which are the first attempt to measure the corpus rather than assume it.

events.title: The Gaekwad Oriental Series begins publishing unpublished manuscripts
events.evidence: The series itself, which printed texts surviving in single copies.

events.title: A critical edition project begins on the Mahabharata
events.evidence: The Bhandarkar Institute's collation of over a thousand manuscripts, which took nearly fifty years.
